summary: 梁冀所立，十五岁即位；延熹二年与宦官诛梁冀，宦官五侯擅政，党锢之祸起于此朝。
summary_en: Raised by Liang Ji, enthroned at fifteen; in Yanxi 2 he destroyed Liang Ji with the eunuchs, the Five Marquises dominated, and the proscription of partisans began in his reign.

bio_md:
# 汉桓帝 · 主要事迹

刘志是蠡吾侯刘翼之子。[[e-han-zhi|质帝]]被鸩后，梁冀迎立年十五的刘志，是为桓帝。此后的十四年，朝政尽在梁冀之手：梁冀一门前后七侯、三皇后、六贵人，专权二十年，百官侧目。

桓帝隐忍十四年，终于延熹二年抓住机会：借宦官单超、徐璜、具瑗、左悺、唐衡五人之力，发兵收梁冀大将军印，梁冀与其妻孙寿皆自杀，梁氏中外宗亲悉诛。然而以宦官诛外戚，代价是宦官集团取代外戚成为新的主宰——单超等五人同日封侯，史称「五侯」，宦官之祸自此转炽。延熹四年财用不足，减公卿以下俸，国力之窘可见一斑。

桓帝朝最深远的事件是党锢之祸：延熹九年，司隶校尉李膺等名士与宦官集团冲突激化，李膺等下狱，第一次党锢起；永康元年虽赦党人归田里，然禁锢终身。士人与宦官的对决，从此成为东汉末年政治的轴心。永康元年十二月，桓帝崩，年三十六，无嗣；窦武迎立解渎亭侯[[e-han-ling|刘宏]]，是为灵帝。史臣谓桓帝「前史残缺，尘垢负涂」，诛梁冀而纵五侯，实开灵帝之世宦官擅权的先声。

> 参考：点校本《后汉书》卷007《孝桓帝纪》、《梁冀传》、《宦者传》、《党锢列传》，谭图第 2 册。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Zhi was the son of the marquis Yi of Liwu. After

was poisoned, Liang Ji raised the fifteen-year-old Zhi to the throne as Emperor Huan. For the next fourteen years the government lay entirely in Liang Ji's hands: his house held seven marquises, three empresses, and six titled ladies, and ruled for twenty years while the ministers looked on askance.

Huan bided his time for fourteen years, and in the second Yanxi year seized his chance: using the eunuchs Shan Chao, Xu Huang, Ju Yuan, Zuo Guan, and Tang Heng, he sent troops to take Liang Ji's seal of office; Liang Ji and his wife Sun Shou killed themselves, and the entire Liang house, kin included, was destroyed. But the cure was worse than the disease: the eunuchs replaced the consorts as the dominant power — Shan Chao and the other four were enfeoffed the same day, the "Five Marquises," and the eunuch scourge burned brighter than ever. In the fourth Yanxi year salaries from the Three Excellencies down were cut for lack of funds — a measure of the realm's straits.

The deepest-reaching event of his reign was the proscription of the partisans: in the ninth Yanxi year the celebrity officials headed by Li Ying, colonel of the capital, clashed head-on with the eunuch faction; Li Ying and others were imprisoned and the first proscription began; in the first Yongkang year the partisans were pardoned and sent home, but barred from office for life. The duel between the scholar-officials and the eunuchs became the axis of late Eastern Han politics from this point on. In the twelfth month of Yongkang 1, Huan died at thirty-six, without issue; Dou Wu raised the marquis of Xieduting,

, as Emperor Ling. The historians wrote that Huan's earlier records are fragmentary and "dirtied with dust" — he destroyed Liang Ji only to unleash the Five Marquises, sounding the prelude to the eunuch autocracy of Ling's reign.

> References: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hou Hanshu*, ch. 7 (Benji of Emperor Huan), and the biographies of Liang Ji, the Eunuchs, and the Proscribed Partisans; Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2.
